To maximize cumulative profit, I must calculate the Expected Value (EV) for each Depth ($d$) using the formula:
$EV = [P(\text{Success}) \times (\text{Revenue} - \text{Fixed Cost})] + [P(\text{Review}) \times (-\text{Recalibration Fee} - \text{Fixed Cost})]$

Given:
- Revenue = $d \times 1000$
- Fixed Cost = 2500
- Recalibration Fee = 2000
- $P(\text{Review}) = 0.05 \times (d/10)^2$
- $P(\text{Success}) = 1 - P(\text{Review})$

Calculations:
- Depth 1: $EV = [1 - 0.0005](1000-2500) + [0.0005](-2000-2500) = -1499.25 - 2.25 = -1501.50$
- Depth 3: $EV = [1 - 0.0045](3000-2500) + [0.0045](-4500) = 497.75 - 20.25 = 477.50$
- Depth 5: $EV = [1 - 0.0125](5000-2500) + [0.0125](-4500) = 2468.75 - 56.25 = 2412.50$
- Depth 7: $EV = [1 - 0.0245](7000-2500) + [0.0245](-4500) = 4389.75 - 110.25 = 4279.50$
- Depth 8: $EV = [1 - 0.032](8000-2500) + [0.032](-4500) = 5324.00 - 144.00 = 5180.00$
- Depth 9: $EV = [1 - 0.0405](9000-2500) + [0.0405](-4500) = 6236.75 - 182.25 = 6054.50$
- Depth 10: $EV = [1 - 0.05](10000-2500) + [0.05](-4500) = 7125.00 - 225.00 = 6900.00$

Depth 10 provides the highest Expected Value per round. Since the Trust Premium is currently $0, there is no financial incentive to lower Depth to 3 or below.

Where:

The Trust Premium is $0, so it does not influence the calculation. The EV increases linearly with Depth because the quadratic risk scaling (max 5%) is insufficient to offset the linear revenue gains within the 1-10 range.
